text: Methodology document: intrinsic calibration of both cameras (ToF SDK intrinsics vs a calibration on the amplitude image), extrinsic ToF-to-RGB calibration feeding the head URDF, time synchronisation of 10 Hz depth with the RGB stream (approximate time, latency budget, pan/tilt motion and rolling-shutter error), registration with occlusion handling, optional RGB-guided upsampling and its validity mask, and the validation procedure with measured reprojection error and depth accuracy.

A C++ fusion node (reusing depth_image_proc where it fits, own code only for what it lacks) publishing an RGB-registered 16UC1 depth image in head_camera_optical_frame (RGB resolution or a configurable fraction), its camera_info and a coloured point cloud at a configurable reduced rate; nothing published without real synchronised inputs and valid TF.
A calibration tool producing the intrinsics and extrinsics files consumed by the node and the head URDF, with tests on synthetic data.

Unit tests for the projection/registration/upsampling maths on synthetic scenes; CPU budget measured on the Pi 5 (Grafana) within 0.2 core; Ansible node type, config, README; deployed and validated on the robot against a target at known distances.
The RTAB-Map epic consumes the registered RGB-D pair from this node (its uplink, server pipeline and status are amended; it is blocked by this epic).
A fusion node registering ToF depth into the RGB camera, publishing a registered depth image, its camera_info and a coloured cloud.
The methodology is written down and measured: calibration, synchronisation, registration, upsampling, validation.
The RTAB-Map epic consumes the registered RGB-D pair from this node.

The head camera keeps continuous autofocus normally and locks focus (about 1 m) only while mapping or fusion consumers need calibrated intrinsics, consistent with the RTAB-Map epic's mapping.lock_focus.
